checks.topic: SDT conditional probabilities and cost accounting
checks.derivation: Inspection probability = pi*(1-P_miss)+(1-pi)*P_fa. Miss harm occurs on uninspected dangers; additional false-alarm burden occurs on inspected safe items; attention cost occurs on every inspected item. C_fa is explicitly additional, so attention is not counted twice. Perfect detection/prevention and at most one inspection are stated; imperfect inspection requires residual harm.

checks.assessment: All displayed values and rounding agree with the stated two-policy model.

With fixed positive pi and finite fixed inspection costs, pi*C_miss diverges while all-inspection cost stays finite. Ratio-only counterexample correctly lets C_fa decrease to zero while miss cost stays fixed; no-inspection cost .001 remains below inspection cost at least1. Reputation has no consequence without a calibrated model connecting it to risk.

Opposite strict slopes establish minima q=0 and q=1. No common q achieves both. Text explicitly limits the counterexample to a common randomized inspection probability and permits class-aware interface settings.

Functions 5*exp(-(x-mu)^2/1.4) have common variance .7 and means3,6. Raw separation arrow is3, not d-prime; standardized separation is3/sqrt(.7). Relative-density axis and arbitrary-scale caption avoid normalized-probability claims. Threshold5 is illustrative; the filled regions are on the correct sides.

Protocol and figure identify two illustrative outcomes, not an exhaustive controller. Other responses need rules; grants remain within independent policy authority. Sandbox prevents direct production mutation, while interruption and future grant effects remain explicitly evaluable. No benefit or ungameability theorem is asserted.

Sentence separates Austin, Searle and FIPA without claiming a direct derivation. Table remains explicitly illustrative, distinguishes request/report/acceptance/completion evidence, and the column change only controls alignment.
